summary: SolsticeRetail on-prem control-plane failover: heartbeat storm, partial audit-log loss, and conversation transcript gaps
description:
Issue summary:
During an automated control-plane certificate rotation on the SolsticeRetail private deployment (onprem-eu-central) the cluster entered an accelerated control-plane failover window. Multiple heartbeat workers started retrying aggressively, producing a 'heartbeat storm' that saturated the local control-plane axis and delayed audit-log flush workers. As a result ~8% of audit-log batches were dropped during the 14:02-14:18 UTC window, and several customer conversation transcripts showed missing tokens or truncated structured-output sections.

Impact:
- Customer observed missing conversation events and truncated transcripts for a subset of sessions (approx 1.2k sessions across peak hour).
- Audit log delivery to Solstice S3 endpoint showed gaps; forensic logs for some requests are incomplete.
- Temporary billing delta: usage accounting replays were required and resulted in an estimated 0.6% invoice exposure for the affected billing period.
- Customer-facing features dependent on audit logs (replay, compliance export) were degraded for ~16 minutes.

Timeline (UTC):
- 13:58 - Scheduled cert rotation begins (orchestrated by private-controlplane-operator).
- 14:02 - First retry cascade observed; heartbeat workers begin exponential retrying earlier than intended due to a regression in backoff config (PR 812).
- 14:03 - Telemetry pipeline lag increases; audit-flush queue length spikes.
- 14:08 - Control-plane API 429 spikes and short-lived 5xx for internal control-plane endpoints.
- 14:18 - Operator circuit-breaker triggers slow-restart sequence; stable quorum reestablished by 14:23.
- 14:30 - Replay and recovery jobs started; partial audit-log repair completed by 17:40.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1. Deploy control-plane operator with the backoff config introduced in PR 812.
2. Trigger cert rotation across a 3-node on-prem cluster with higher-than-usual clock skew between nodes (emulated).
3. Observe heartbeat workers shift into rapid-retry mode, control-plane API rate-limits, and audit-flush worker timeouts.

Logs / Observations:
- control-plane (node-1): repeated "heartbeat: retrying after 50ms" logs at 14:02:12 followed by "rate-limited write: audit-flush-failed" messages.
- telemetry: "flush worker drop_count=124" during 14:03-14:18 window.
- serving-runtime: transient transcript truncation traces (request IDs provided to customer via secure channel).
- audit-forwarder: upstream S3 putObject errors with "connection reset by peer" correlated to local IO timeout at 14:05.

Mitigation & Resolution:
- Immediate mitigation: Support disabled automatic cert rotation for Solstice private control plane while SRE rolled back backoff config to the previous safe profile.
- SRE applied a hotfix to heartbeat worker backoff (reverted PR 812 logic) at 14:12 which reduced retry amplification.
- Operator circuit-breaker tuning reverted to conservative thresholds at 14:20; cluster quorum recovered by 14:23.
- Audit-log repair: replay job rebuilt ~92% of missing events using transactionally consistent request logs and local buffering. Remaining ~8% were marked as unrecoverable and documented.
- Billing correction: Finance issued a 0.6% credit for the affected billing window; an action item to automate credit detection created.

Root cause hypothesis:
- A regression in control-plane operator backoff behavior (PR 812) reduced base backoff and disabled jitter under certain clock skew conditions on on-prem clusters. When cert rotation induced short-term control-plane contention, heartbeat workers entered synchronized rapid retries, amplifying load and causing audit-flush timeouts. A secondary factor was an aggressive circuit-breaker threshold which preferred restart over graceful throttling.

Customer communication & impact notes:
- Solstice Retail Engineering and Security teams were notified at 14:10 and included in incident bridge.
- We provided secure request IDs and a per-session list of affected transcripts.
- Customer requested retention of recovered audit events and a signed attestation of the recovery process for compliance; we delivered the attestation and replay logs by 2026-03-12.

Post-incident actions (owner tags in parentheses):
- Roll back PR 812 in private-controlplane-operator and publish hotfix release (SRE - Diego Martinez) - done 2026-03-10 14:12.
- Add jitter and minimum backoff guardrails to heartbeat worker config and add unit tests (Runtime - Priya Singh) - in progress.
- Improve operator circuit-breaker to prefer throttling over restart in transient pressure scenarios (Infra - Jonah Liu) - scheduled.
- Implement audit-log integrity check and retry telemetry to surface early drop signals (Telemetry - Marina Kovac) - TODO.
- Create automated billing-delta detector to flag invoice exposure within 24 hours of incident (Finance Eng - Omar Reed) - TODO.
- Deliver customer attestation and supplemental logs (CS - Aisha Patel) - done 2026-03-12.

Follow-up deadlines:
- Config guardrails merged by 2026-03-17.
- Circuit-breaker tuning rollout canary by 2026-03-20.
- Audit integrity monitoring v1 by 2026-03-27.

Resolution summary:
- Incident declared resolved after hotfix rollback and audit-log repair (partial). Customer operations restored and compliance artifacts delivered. Finance processed a targeted credit for affected usage. Long-term mitigations prioritized and owners assigned.

Notes on customer sensitivity:
- Customer is PCI-scoped and requires signed attestations for any data repair; we have preserved chain-of-custody for recovered artifacts and engaged our security/compliance team.

Attachments provided to customer (via secure SFTP): list of request IDs, partial replay manifests, signed attestation PDF.
